clue.text: Woodcutter some know as GI Joe is coming west

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming west means travelling right to left, so the run is read backwards
some of the letters of the phrase know as GI Joe are taken as a run

explanation.surface: A soldier nicknamed GI Joe is heading west, known among friends as a lumberjack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks the run WASGIJ from 'know as GI Joe'; 'coming west' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigsaw is a fine saw for cutting curves, so it is literally a tool that cuts wood.

clue.text: Follower of India with best headgear for match

parts.note: in the NATO phonetic alphabet Juliet comes straight after India
to best someone is to cap or outdo them

explanation.surface: Whoever comes after India in the batting order wears the best helmet for the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' here is a wedding, not a sporting fixture: the small close-fitting cap is often worn by brides.
explanation.definitionFit: A Juliet cap is a small netted skullcap traditionally worn by brides, so it is headwear for a marriage.

clue.text: Irritated after serving American some meat

indicators.note: after places the word for irritated behind the American soldier

parts.note: a GI is an American serviceman
something that got to you, or simply got you, irritated you

explanation.surface: A US serviceman, annoyed, is handed a portion of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigot is a leg of mutton or lamb, a particular cut of meat.

clue.text: Fired partner involved in a racket that's come up

indicators.note: involved in means set inside the following letters
in a down clue, coming up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: din is a racket, a loud noise
a mate is a partner or companion

explanation.surface: A colleague has been dismissed after becoming caught up in a scam that has come to light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' looks like sacked, but it means fired up; the reversal indicator 'that's come up' applies only to the racket.
explanation.definitionFit: Fired in the sense of fired up or enthused is a synonym for lively and spirited.

clue.text: Helping bank, can put in a grand

indicators.note: put in signals that the following letters are placed inside

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
to bank on something is to bet on it
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A bank, it seems, can deposit a thousand to help out.
explanation.definitionFit: Abetting is assisting or aiding, usually in wrongdoing, so it means helping.

clue.text: Keeps springing up in the field of children's entertainment

definitions.text: Keeps springing up in the field of children's entertainment

parts.words: Keeps springing up in the field of children's entertainment
parts.note: keeps are castle towers, and springing suggests bounciness; these inflatable play structures appear in fields at children's parties

explanation.definitionFit: Inflatable play castles are a staple of children's parties and fairs, often set up in a field.

clue.text: Dry clothes lifted by gangster, killer of Montague

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the dry letters dress or surround the rest

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, which is dry in the sense of abstaining from drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the small word reads upwards

parts.note: Al Capone is the stock crossword gangster

explanation.surface: A gangster has stolen dry laundry, a crime worthy of a Shakespearean villain.
explanation.walkthrough: In Romeo and Juliet Tybalt, a Capulet, kills Mercutio, Romeo's friend; 'lifted' works on the little word 'by' itself, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Tybalt is the Capulet swordsman in Romeo and Juliet who kills a Montague ally, Mercutio, in a duel.

clue.text: Batting second, one plays wide, swerving delivery

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in
a winger is a player who plays out wide on the flank

explanation.surface: A batsman goes in second while a fielder plays wide of a swinging ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an inswinger is a ball that curves in the air towards the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: An inswinger is a cricket ball that curves in towards the batsman, a swerving delivery.

clue.text: Gun keeping face, not bottom, in range

indicators.note: keeping means holding the next letters inside

parts.note: gat is old slang for a gun

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter, which is dropped

parts.note: mug is slang for face

explanation.surface: A gun that keeps one's face, though not one's backside, within range.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the bottom of a word is its final letter, so 'not bottom' trims the face word at its end.
explanation.definitionFit: The gamut is the full range or scope of something, from one extreme to the other.

clue.text: Toiling away with spades working in forest

indicators.note: away with means get rid of the letter that follows

parts.note: slogging is toiling, working hard
S is the abbreviation for spades in card games

explanation.surface: Labouring away with spades while working in a wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away with spades' removes S from the front of SLOGGING.
explanation.definitionFit: Logging is the felling and cutting of trees, the work done in a forest.

clue.text: Fine imposed on any one of eight in plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, imposed on puts the first word above the second

parts.note: good means fine
England has had eight kings named Henry, so any of them is a King Henry

explanation.surface: A fine was levied on one of eight people in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like a penalty and 'plant' like a factory; Good King Henry is a herb related to spinach.
explanation.definitionFit: Good King Henry is a perennial herb of the goosefoot family, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Parisian's one bowing out initially, so minutes reveal

parts.note: un is French for one

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A Frenchman bows out early, and so the minutes reveal it.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbosom is to disclose one's secrets or feelings, to reveal what is in one's heart.

clue.text: Old artist capturing the head of Thomas More

indicators.note: capturing means holding the next letter inside

parts.note: ex means former or old
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A former painter has captured the likeness of Sir Thomas More.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thomas More' looks like a single name; More is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means more, additional to what is usual.

clue.text: Ornate stucco tile cut for black artist

indicators.note: ornate suggests elaborate rearrangement of the letters
cut signals that the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A fancy stucco tile is trimmed for a black artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims TILE to TIL; 'Ornate' then rearranges STUCCO and TIL.
explanation.definitionFit: An occultist practises the black arts of magic and the supernatural.

clue.text: It causes excitement where sides meet

definitions.text: It causes excitement where sides meet

parts.words: It causes excitement where sides meet
parts.note: a kick is excitement and a corner is where two sides meet; in football this set piece is taken from the corner of the pitch and causes excitement in the goalmouth

explanation.definitionFit: In football this set piece is taken from the corner flag, where touchline and goal line meet.

clue.text: The blue half of Merseyside for example?

definitions.text: The blue half of Merseyside for example?

parts.words: The blue half of Merseyside for example?
parts.note: blue is the Conservative colour, standing for the political right, and one side of the Mersey river is one of its banks

explanation.walkthrough: 'The blue half of Merseyside' suggests Everton FC; Merseyside is the area round Liverpool on the river Mersey.
explanation.definitionFit: A river has a left and a right side when facing downstream; either one is a bank.

clue.text: Rob marketplace of old Indian city

indicators.note: rob means take away from, so the letter is removed

parts.note: an agora was a marketplace in ancient Greece

explanation.surface: Thieves robbed a market in an ancient city of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra is a city in Uttar Pradesh, India, home of the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: Badly shaken by extreme letters to one Jew

indicators.note: badly means the letters are messed up

parts.note: A and Z are the letters at either end of the alphabet
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone badly shaken by threatening letters to a Jewish man.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ashkenazi is a Jew of central or eastern European descent.

clue.text: Making one's own way down the mountain?

definitions.text: Making one's own way down the mountain?

parts.words: Making one's own way down the mountain?
parts.note: a skier who leaves the groomed runs chooses their own route down the slope

explanation.definitionFit: Skiing away from the prepared runs is skiing on unmarked snow, choosing your own route.

clue.text: Plough on with leader of each pair in dance

indicators.note: split the words into pairs of letters and take the first of each pair

explanation.surface: Ploughing on while each pair of dancers takes the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: PL OU GH ON gives P, O, G, O.
explanation.definitionFit: The pogo is a punk dance in which you jump straight up and down.

clue.text: Odd sort of hand, etc

indicators.note: odd means peculiar, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange kind of hand of cards, and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: Etc is short for et cetera, meaning and the rest of that kind.

clue.text: High King visiting region with daughter

indicators.note: visiting means going inside the following word

parts.note: a zone is a region
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king tours an area with his daughter, feeling elated.
explanation.definitionFit: Zonked is slang for intoxicated, high on drugs or drink.

clue.text: Girl to go off Prince? This won't happen!

definitions.text: Girl to go off Prince? This won't happen!

parts.note: Bet is a girl's name, short for Elizabeth
to rot is to go off or decay
Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: If a young woman goes off her prince, the wedding is off.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines it: if the girl goes off the prince, the engagement will not go ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A betrothal is an engagement to marry, the very thing cancelled when a girl falls out of love.

clue.text: Saint overwhelmed by blessing a tiny bit

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means swallowed up inside the following word

parts.note: a boon is a blessing

explanation.surface: A saint is overwhelmed by a blessing, just a little.
explanation.walkthrough: A tiny bit here is a subatomic particle.
explanation.definitionFit: A boson is a subatomic particle, such as the photon, so literally a tiny bit of matter.

clue.text: Lawmen have to abandon ship only once

indicators.note: to abandon means leave behind, so the letters are dropped
only once says only one of the two pairs of letters is removed

parts.note: to possess is to have
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Sheriffs must leave the boat just this one time.
explanation.walkthrough: POSSESS has two SS pairs; dropping only one leaves POSSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a band of men summoned by a sheriff to enforce the law.

clue.text: Being member of students' union upset Moslem

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down, reading them backwards

parts.note: being a member of a group is being in it
the NUS is the UK National Union of Students

explanation.surface: A Muslim member of the students' union is upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sunni is a member of the larger of the two main branches of Islam.

clue.text: Senate entertaining need to reduce tension

indicators.note: entertaining means taking in as a guest, so the other word goes inside

parts.note: Sen is an abbreviation for senate or senator
lack means need or want

explanation.surface: The Senate takes on the need to ease strained relations.
explanation.definitionFit: To slacken a rope is to loosen it, reducing its tension.

clue.text: Her story is apocryphal — suspicion record incomplete

parts.note: sus is British slang for suspicion

indicators.note: incomplete signals losing the last letter

parts.note: an annal is a record of events

explanation.surface: A doubtful tale whose record is unfinished, so it is suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: The Story of Susanna is one of the books of the Apocrypha.
explanation.definitionFit: The tale of Susanna and the Elders is an addition to Daniel found in the biblical Apocrypha.

clue.text: View not helped by the presence of bins, perhaps

definitions.text: View not helped by the presence of bins, perhaps

parts.words: View not helped by the presence of bins, perhaps
parts.note: bins is British slang for binoculars; looking without any optical aid is seeing unassisted

explanation.walkthrough: 'bins' suggests rubbish bins spoiling a view; here it is short for binoculars.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaided human vision, with no telescope or binoculars, is called seeing with this.

clue.text: Imagine Variety without a lot of stars

indicators.note: variety signals a rearrangement, and without says one letter is first left out

explanation.surface: Picture a variety show without a lot of the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: IMAGINE without A gives IMGINE, rearranged as the constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini is a constellation, the Twins, and a constellation is a group of stars.
